recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The original implementer-facing frame-reference requirement is already represented in current source, and reintroducing the old FrameSet/retrieveUrl model would conflict with later resource redesigns; future frame retrieval changes should be handled as new ImagingSelection issues.
issue_request: FHIR-3843 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It requested a frame component under ImagingObjectSelection.instance for multi-frame DICOM SOP instances, with frame numbers and retrieval URL support, and also requested removal of retrieveAETitle from series and instance.
initial_application: Historical commit a51afaf7a9 applied the issue to the then-current ImagingObjectSelection spreadsheet and example by removing retrieveAETitle, renaming retrieveUrl to url, and adding instance frames with frameNumbers and a retrieval URL.
additional_context: ImagingObjectSelection is no longer an active resource in the current build; source/fhir.ini marks ImagingSelection active and approved and marks ImagingObjectSelection dropped. Later related work renamed the old plural frame element names, restored frame references after the ImagingManifest transition, and introduced the current ImagingSelection resource, which uses instance.frameNumber plus endpoint-based retrieval guidance rather than the original FrameSet/retrieveUrl shape.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The active ImagingSelection StructureDefinition defines ImagingSelection.instance.frameNumber as a 0..* positiveInt list of selected frames from a multiframe SOP Instance, and the notes and multiframe example use frameNumber consistently.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue that renamed the old plural frames/frameNumbers element names to singular frame/number.
Later Published issue that identified the same frame-reference gap after ImagingObjectSelection was replaced by ImagingManifest; already represented on the combined branch.
Later Published issue that introduced the active ImagingSelection resource now carrying the frame-reference capability; already represented on the combined branch.
